oewn-01251399-n.learner: the act of starting something again, or of making it new again.
examples: She would not even wish for any renewal of his attentions.
How could I ever be foolish enough to expect a renewal of his love?

oewn-13569128-n.learner: the act of filling something up again by adding more of what has been used up.
examples: The camp needed a steady renewal of its food and fuel through the winter.

oewn-00269862-n.learner: the work of turning waste land into land where people can live or grow crops.
examples: After years of renewal, the waste ground by the river was ready for farms and houses.

oewn-04754685-n.learner: the way two things are alike in how they look, or in small outward details.
examples: When, after examining the mother, in whose countenance and deportment she soon found some resemblance of Mr. Darcy, she turned her eyes on the daughter
as he looked at her, he was trying to trace a resemblance.

oewn-01849662-v.learner: to go on a journey or a trip.
examples: business with his steward had occasioned his coming forward a few hours before the rest of the party with whom he had been travelling.
They travelled as expeditiously as possible; and sleeping one night on the road, reached Longbourn by dinnertime the next day.

oewn-01839438-v.learner: to move, go, or go forward from one place to another, also in a figurative way.
examples: News of the wedding travelled fast through the village.
Sound travels more slowly than light.

oewn-01846997-v.learner: to go on a trip because you enjoy it.
examples: When they stopped working, they travelled just for fun, seeing a new country every year.

oewn-01845021-v.learner: to be carried from place to place, as in a car, coach, or other vehicle.
examples: I cannot bear the idea of two young women travelling post by themselves.
We travelled north on the night train.

oewn-01850858-v.learner: to go along or across a place, such as a road or a sea.
examples: Few ships travel this stretch of sea in winter.

oewn-02106280-v.learner: to go from place to place, for example to find work, to preach, or to act as a judge.
examples: The judge travelled from town to town to hear cases.

oewn-00933531-a.learner: not thought likely to happen, or not looked for ahead of time.
examples: On the very day of my coming home from Longbourn, your uncle had a most unexpected visitor.
This is wholly unexpected; I had not an idea of it.

oewn-02531751-v.learner: to get or reach something by working hard for it.
examples: After years of saving, she finally accomplished her dream of owning a small farm.

oewn-01644397-v.learner: to carry something out so that it really happens.
examples: The soldiers accomplished the orders exactly as they were given.
With the job accomplished, she went home to rest.

oewn-02136915-s.learner: firmly fixed and no longer open to doubt, with no conditions attached.
examples: By the time her family heard of it, the marriage was an accomplished fact.

oewn-02113646-s.learner: aware of something, used with 'to' or 'of'.
examples: She was more alive to the disgrace, which her want of new clothes must reflect on her daughter's nuptials
The bird was still alive when we found it.

oewn-00930614-s.learner: working or going on; in use.
examples: The old custom was kept alive in the village for many years.

oewn-00041710-s.learner: able to erupt, as a volcano still can.
examples: Scientists say the volcano is still alive and could erupt again.

oewn-05149888-n.learner: something that helps a person or makes their life better.
examples: I have often observed how little young ladies are interested by books of a serious stamp, though written solely for their benefit.
the true philosopher will derive benefit from such as are given.

oewn-13317922-n.learner: money given to help people at a time when they are in need.
examples: After losing his job, he lived on a small benefit until he found work.

oewn-06905573-n.learner: a show or concert given to raise money for a charity or good cause.
examples: The band played a benefit for the children's hospital.

oewn-02609706-v.learner: to be real and present in the world, or to still be around.
examples: There could not exist in the world two men over whom Mr. Darcy could have such boundless influence.
You supposed more than really existed.

oewn-02622766-v.learner: to keep yourself going and get what you need to live.
examples: For a whole year the students existed on bread and cheap soup.
You mean to frighten me, Mr. Darcy, by coming in all this state to hear me.
There is a stubbornness about me that never can bear to be frightened at the will of others.
